title: A subgraph's title is placed clear of the routes crossing its band, diverging from Mermaid 12

v:
## Context

Mermaid 12.2.0 centres a subgraph's title across the top of its frame. ELK puts the cluster's first members under that title, and an edge entering or leaving the subgraph through the top runs straight through the band, so the line crosses the title's words. On the 11 flowchart parity fixtures, Mermaid 12.2.0 draws 22 edges through a title. Siren on ELK drew 25.

Measured with elkjs 0.9.3 on small TB, BT, LR and nested graphs, ELK has no native way to keep routes off the title:

| Candidate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Title as the cluster's node label (`[H_CENTER, V_TOP, INSIDE]`, `nodeSize.constraints [NODE_LABELS]`, with or without `nodeLabels.padding` and `spacing.labelNode`) | ELK places the label in the band and routes straight through it; through-titles unchanged. Under DOWN/UP the frame is sized from the rotated label (the bug described in `clusterShape`'s doc) unless a `MINIMUM_SIZE` floor is added. |
| Explicit NORTH ports on the frame for the edge entering the cluster (`portConstraints` `FIXED_SIDE`, `FIXED_ORDER`, `FIXED_POS`) | Under `INCLUDE_CHILDREN`, ELK places each port in line with the member it leads to, whatever position is given. |
| The same with `FIXED_RATIO` | The engine throws. |
| A title-sized child node | ELK gives it a slot in the first layer beside the members, not a band above them. The fitted frame no longer holds it. |

## Decision

The shared layout core moves only the title (`placeTitlesClear` in `layout/directedGraph/layoutDirectedGraph.ts`). Post-layout passes live in the core, per rule 2 of `01M4VANRC6B2C14NHVC2KRZ9Y8`. The pass runs after `fitFrames` and `straightenTerminals`, before the line hops. It changes no route and no frame.

The rule, for each titled cluster:

- Every route segment that reaches into the title's height blocks its horizontal extent, widened by half the cluster's padding.
- If the centred title clears every blocked stretch, it stays centred.
- Otherwise the title moves to the place nearest the centre that clears every blocked stretch. That place stays at the band's height, with the title at least half a padding inside the frame's sides.
- If no place fits, the title stays centred. The frame is never widened, because frames come from ELK and `fitFrames`.

The band is across the frame's top in every direction (`clusterShape`), so the same rule holds for TB, BT, LR and RL.

This diverges from Mermaid 12 under rule 1 of `01M4VANRC6B2C14NHVC2KRZ9Y8`. A line through a title's words makes the title hard to read.

## Evidence

Parity, 11 flowchart fixtures, Siren against Mermaid 12.2.0 in headless Chrome. Through-titles fall from 25 to 15. Every other gate metric is identical before and after:

| Metric | Before | After | Mermaid |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Through-titles | 25 | 15 | 22 |
| Crossings | 176 | 176 | 176 |
| Through-nodes | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Vertical agreement (pooled) | 99.56% | 99.56% | — |
| Horizontal agreement (pooled) | 97.82% | 97.82% | — |
| Failures | 0 | 0 | — |
| Reversals | 34 | 34 | 31 |
| Mean detour (average of the per-fixture means) | 1.207 | 1.207 | 1.203 |

Reversals and detour cannot move, because the routes are untouched.

Through-titles per fixture, Siren before → after:

| Fixture | Siren before → after | Mermaid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| garden-network | 6 → 5 | 7 |
| street-fair | 5 → 4 | 5 |
| dense-24 | 1 → 1 | 0 |
| dense-36 | 5 → 2 | 5 |
| dense-50 | 6 → 1 | 3 |
| example-flowchart-edges | 1 → 1 | 1 |
| subgraph-direction-crossing | 1 → 1 | 1 |
| All others | 0 → 0 | 0 |

The edges that still run through a title cross frames with no free place in the band: frames no wider than the title and its padding, or bands crossed by several routes.

Core tests (`layoutDirectedGraph.test.ts`):

- "places a group's title clear of the routes crossing its band": the title goes beside the route when the frame has room. It stays centred when nothing crosses the band, and when no place fits.
- "frames a group > with the title's centre in the band, clear of every route crossing the band, inside the frame by half a padding".

## Alternatives rejected

**Taking routes round the title, inside the band.** A vertical run turned aside before the title, past the title's end, and back into line. Measured on the same fixtures:

- Through-titles fell to 6.
- Reversals rose from 34 to 42.
- Mean detour rose from 1.21 to 1.26.
- Without a rule giving each detour a lane of its own, crossings also rose from 176 to 212: routes into one member shared a lane and their rounded corners met.

Rejected because reversals and detour got worse. The authorization requires that no other metric worsens, and lines that head sideways and come back are what this migration exists to remove. In the rendered pictures, the detours run along the frame's top border and jog out and back.

**Sliding the title with a fallback to the least-crossed place when no place clears every route.** Not taken. A title moved only part of the way still sits on a line, and the centred title is Mermaid's.

## Consequences

When a route crosses a subgraph's band and the frame has room, the subgraph's title is no longer centred. It sits beside the routes, as near the centre as they allow. Where the frame has no room, the title stays centred and still has a line through it, as in Mermaid. Class, state and ER diagrams get the same treatment when they move onto ELK.
